conviction_note: No unpriced company-level number found. The evidence is mixed and mostly proxies: Q2 buyback acceleration and the post-quarter authorisation raise (positive), a seasonally slow July with a Virginia hangover set against a consensus that was revised up about 7% (negative), Q3 adjusted NICS +2.5%, and the name's five-for-five record of rising on its prints. That gives a weak up-lean, p_up 55, on an abs move of 7.5 taken from the historical median of 6.1 (no usable chain). impact_sum +0.7 and the scaled +0.75 agree because neither has much in it.
bar: Revenue about $13.16M and EPS $0.01 for the Nov 16 2026 quarter, revenue estimate revised up 7.05% in 3 months. One source only (Chartmill, POWWP preferred page: https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/POWWP/estimates, seen via search snippet; the direct fetch returned 403). The common-stock MarketBeat consensus is stale. The company gives no numeric guidance. So the bar is effectively unsourced and every finding is capped small. Prior-year comparison: Q2 FY26 revenue $11.98M, adj EBITDA $4.91M, net income from continuing ops $1.40M (https://www.itiger.com/news/2582995873, https://finviz.com/news/224322/outdoor-holding-company-reports-positive-net-income-from-continuing-operations-for-second-quarter-fiscal-2026). $13.16M is +9.9% YoY. With a take rate of about 6.5% (legacy 6.08% plus about 0.4pt of FFL fees) against about 6.34% a year ago, it implies GMV of about $202M, roughly +7% YoY.
positioning_check: Short interest 2.56M shares, about 2.2% of shares outstanding, 4.46 days to cover, FINRA settlement 2026-10-30 (https://equibles.com/stocks/poww/shortinterest, via the sweep row). Not crowded. No skew: the chain is unusable (ATM not two-sided, total OI 399, put/call OI 0.11). Spot $2.31: 5-day run-up +0.4%, 20-day +6.0%, 9.8% below the 52-week high and 42.6% above the 52-week low. All 5 prior prints moved up (median 6.13%, max +20.19% on 2026-08-10). The CEO/Chairman (Urvan) holds 27.5% including warrants (13D/A 2026-08-14), so the free float is smaller than shares outstanding.

findings.finding: The buyback accelerated in fiscal Q2 and was enlarged after quarter end. Through 2026-09-30 the company had repurchased 3,975,951 shares for about $8.4M in total. At the Aug 10 call the figure was about 1.5M shares since January at $1.97 average. That puts roughly 2.5M shares and about $5.4M in Jul-Sep, against $2.0M in Q1. On 2026-10-19, with Q2 closed, the board raised the authorisation from $15M to $35M and extended it to 2027-07-04. Market cap is about $270M and cash was $68.8M at June 30.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on the buyback alone. The Aug 10 print, which carried Q1's first $2M of repurchases with a strong quarter, rose +20.19%. The Oct 22 8-K produced no visible separate jump: 20-day run-up is +6%.
findings.why_not_priced: The 8-K is public, so the authorisation itself is priced. The Q2 pace (about 2% of shares retired in one quarter) and what it implies about cash generation will only show in the Q2 10-Q/release with the share count and operating cash flow. If the market had read a board raising the program by 133% with the quarter's numbers in hand as a confidence signal, the stock would be at the 52-week high, not 9.8% under it.
findings.independence: The Aug 10 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15419276080137216) gives the 1.5M-share / $1.97 figure since January that the Q2 pace is derived from. Same company, different document.

findings.finding: Industry demand in the fiscal quarter was modest. NSSF-adjusted NICS for Jul-Sep 2026 was 3,329,270, +2.5% YoY; September alone was 1,152,077, -2.3%. Q1 FY27 ran at +5.3%, and in that quarter GunBroker firearm units grew +11.6% and GMV +18.1%. To reach the ~$13.16M bar, GMV must grow about 7% (the FFL transfer fee lifts the take rate about 2.5%), so GunBroker needs about 4-5 points of share outperformance over NICS. That is plausible on Q1's ex-Virginia gap of about +12% GMV, but not a beat signal.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On Aug 10, GMV +18% against NICS +5% rose +20.19%. Last November, GMV -1.1% (flat revenue) with a return to profit rose +6.13%. The stock has risen on all 5 prints whatever the GMV growth.
findings.why_not_priced: NICS is public and the two covering analysts (Roth, Lake Street) will have it. The only thing possibly not priced is the deceleration from Q1's +5.3% to +2.5% after a 7% upward revision to the revenue estimate. A fully priced slowdown would show as a cut estimate, and the estimate went up.
findings.independence: Industry proxy, not company data. Sturm Ruger's Q3 (https://www.panabee.com/news/sturm-ruger-earnings-q3-2026) is a manufacturer and points the other way on revenue (+16.5%); it is filed separately.

findings.finding: Management told the Aug 10 call that July is the slowest time of year and that the Virginia law's timing caused a dip in July buying, with shoppers going back to brick-and-mortar stores. It said it is not assuming Q1's Virginia pull-forward repeats in Q2. Virginia's ban was enjoined statewide from July 21 (Santolla v. Katz, through 2027-07-01), so no fresh deadline-driven buying arrived. Against that, the one available revenue estimate was revised up 7% in three months.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Management flagged the Virginia caveat in the Aug 10 release and the stock still rose +20.19% that day. No prior print shows a hangover quarter after a legislative pull-forward.
findings.why_not_priced: The caveat is public, but the estimate moved up rather than down after it (Chartmill snippet). If the July dip were priced, the bar would sit nearer flat-to-+5% YoY than +10%. The bar is single-sourced, so this is capped small.
findings.independence: Virginia injunction timeline from a separate source: https://www.wdbj7.com/2026/07/08/judge-rules-virginia-gun-law-injunctions-apply-statewide/ . It shares the call transcript with the opex and margin finding (different statements).

findings.finding: Cost base and margin should lift profit YoY whatever happens to GMV. Q1 opex was $8.9M, which the CFO called 'definitely a better run rate for the normalized business'. FFL transfer implementation costs were finished in May and are not expected to recur, and gross margin was guided to stabilise above 85% (Q1 84.5%). Prior-year Q2 had adj EBITDA of $4.91M and net income from continuing ops of $1.40M. Revenue of about $13.2M at 85% gross margin less about $9M of opex gives roughly $2.2-2.5M of operating income and adj EBITDA of about $6.5-7.5M (+35-50% YoY), or about $0.01-0.02 per common share after $0.77M of preferred dividends, against a $0.01 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Profitability surprises have been bought. Nov 2025's first profit from continuing ops rose +6.13%; Aug 2026 adj EBITDA of $7.9M vs $3.1M rose +20.19%.
findings.why_not_priced: This sits inside what management already told the market (run-rate opex, margin above 85%), so it is a guided reported-quarter item and sized toward zero. What may not be priced is the size of the YoY EBITDA step on a stock most aggregators still show at a negative or $0.01 EPS bar. If it were, the EPS consensus would read $0.02, not $0.01.
findings.independence: The Aug 10 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15419276080137216) carries the CFO's statements; it is the same quarter's disclosure, read once.

findings.finding: NFA-item demand surged. September 2026 NFA checks were 149,614, +129% YoY. On the Aug 10 call the CFO said NFA items on GunBroker were 'up quite a bit quarter-over-quarter' (the transcript's figure, around 50%, is garbled). The ATF's Oct 9 move away from registration and approval for suppressors and short-barreled firearms, which falls inside the current quarter, gives management a tailwind to cite on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print has turned on NFA items; the line has never been broken out.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (article on September 2026 NICS; page date not confirmed beyond the October path of the related ammoland URL https://www.ammoland.com/2026/10/september-2026-gun-sales-nics-nfa-checks/)
findings.why_not_priced: NFA items are a small share of GunBroker GMV and no estimate models them. A priced NFA tailwind would show as the Q3 estimate moving up, and nothing aggregates that. It is a proxy whose transmission to GMV the company has only described qualitatively, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: CFO comment on the Aug 10 call: https://www.webull.com/news/15419276080137216 (company-level, qualitative).

findings.finding: A peer reporting after GunBroker last spoke had a stronger quarter. Sturm Ruger's Q3 2026 net sales were $147.6M, +16.5% YoY (adj EPS $0.44 vs $0.10). Its year-to-date distributor sell-through was +5%, after Q2 sell-through of +19% against NICS +5%. That suggests firearm retail demand through the summer was firmer than the -2.3% September NICS print alone implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of POWW reacting to a peer's print.
findings.why_not_priced: Manufacturer shipments, which include new products and channel fill, are a narrow proxy for a used-heavy online marketplace, and the broad NICS series (+2.5%) is filed beside it. It is sized below that series by rule.
findings.independence: Contradicted in part by the broader NICS series in the second finding; the Ruger release was not fetchable (403) and is read from the search snippet and https://www.panabee.com/news/sturm-ruger-earnings-q3-2026.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The mild up-lean matches the name's five-for-five record of rising on prints and the +6% 20-day run-up, so whatever up-lean exists is partly in the price already.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6: the bar has one source (Chartmill preferred page), so every finding was capped smaller. Buyback +0.8 to +0.6, NICS -0.3 to -0.2, the July/Virginia-vs-revised-bar finding -0.6 to -0.4 (it leans on that same unsourced revision), NFA +0.4 to +0.3.
Lesson 6 / core table: the opex and margin finding sits inside what management already told the market (run-rate opex, gross margin above 85%), so it moved toward zero, +0.6 to +0.4.
Lesson 5: Ruger is a narrow manufacturer proxy that partly contradicts the broad NICS series, so it was sized below that series, +0.2 to +0.1.

Lessons 8 and core 3b: no unpriced company-level number exists, so abs_move was not raised for thin coverage beyond the understatement correction (6.1 median to 7.5); print_vs_bar trimmed from +1.5 to +1.0 given the unsourced bar.
Left standing: the warrant finding (-0.1), p_up 55, and the decision to file the near-zero proxies rather than drop them.
